A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PLUS and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite retitling and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model accuracy, generalization experiments, and GPT-4 personalization results in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds component ablations, conversation-only evaluations, training curves, and revised response-generation results.

M1.justification: Both versions co-train a PPO summarizer and a summary-conditioned reward model, then use summaries for preference prediction and personalized generation. v2 expands the mathematical and procedural description without establishing a different operational algorithm; the displayed reward-sign correction preserves v1's stated loss-minimizing intent.

E1.justification: Pets, Pets OOD, UltraFeedback-P2/P4, and PRISM remain. v2 Table 4 adds a distinct conversation-only context scenario using chosen responses without rejected responses, extending evaluation beyond preference-pair histories within the existing UltraFeedback coverage.

E2.justification: The principal BTL, DPL, VPL, ICL, PLUS-untrained, and oracle comparator suite remains. Targeted additions include frozen-reward-model and GPT-4o-summary controls in Table 3 and ICL in the existing user-guideline experiment in Table 4. GPT-4-turbo disappears from the response-generation comparison.

E3.justification: Response generation changes from 100 held-out conversations to unseen-user evaluation: v2 Section 6.6 specifies two prompts for each of 308 users, while Appendix E instead states 906 prompts. New ablations introduce frozen components and a 1.5B reward model. Reported PPO settings also change, including critic learning rate from 9e-6 to 9e-7 and PRISM KL coefficient from 0.01 to 0.001. These are reported protocol revisions, not proof that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands tests of co-adaptation through frozen-component and GPT-4o-summary controls, broadens input ablations to conversation-only histories, and adds PRISM training curves and personalization examples. Conversely, v1's dedicated 307-conversation controversial-response evaluation and PRISM profile-augmentation analysis disappear. Existing Pets OOD and held-out-user PRISM analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 explicitly identifies entries without standard deviations as single-seed results, including larger-model results whose v1 Table 2 lacked a run-count statement. Conversely, v1's explicit single-seed disclosure for PRISM is absent from the relocated results. Existing three-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting remains; no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial ablation results, including conversation-only PLUS accuracies of 68.3 and 62.45 versus ICL's 58.55 and 56.96 on UF-P2/P4. Generation results are replaced: personalized/default win rates become 72/28 for GPT-4o and 69/31 for GPT-4.1, versus 66/34 and 59/38 in v1, under changed evaluation sets. Most retained benchmark scores match, but ICL's Llama UF-P2 accuracy changes from 59.40 to 59.10. Profile-augmentation and controversy-only results are removed.

T1.justification: v1 Algorithm 1 writes the summarizer reward as -L = -log sigma despite describing prediction-loss minimization. v2 Equations 3–4 consistently distinguish negative-log-likelihood loss from the log-sigma return, correcting this sign inconsistency. Other added PPO equations largely formalize the existing procedure; neither version supplies a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about co-adaptation, interpretable summaries, robustness, and transfer remain. v2 adds an explicit priority claim for PRISM reward-modeling results and foregrounds superiority to GPT-4o-generated summaries. Its headline evidence shifts from 3–10% gains on UltraFeedback/PRISM to 11–77% over BTL on Pets/UltraFeedback and a 72% personalized GPT-4o win rate.

C2.justification: v2 adds an expressivity and sample-complexity explanation for compression in Appendix A and interprets frozen-component results as support for co-adaptation. Section 6.5 explicitly states the assumption of stable preferences across conversation topics. Appendix F retains the PRISM generalization limitation while distinguishing weak reward-model accuracy from useful GPT-4 response personalization.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands PPO documentation with GAE parameters, clipping, reward range, KL estimator, warmup, microbatch sizes, Adam coefficients, and detailed update pseudocode. However, it drops v1's VPL epoch counts, separate summarizer batch sizes, and per-method L40 allocations, while describing computation using four H200 GPUs. Dataset sizes and prompt templates are largely retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens research positioning through a taxonomy of personalized reward modeling versus response personalization, coverage of Group Preference Optimization, MallowsPO and shared-LoRA approaches, and a dedicated summarization literature discussion. New multi-agent RL references support the PPO rationale. The central distinctions from VPL and RLPF remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. The question-led method narrative becomes an objective-based account; domains and baselines reverse order; results are reorganized; and the conclusion becomes a discussion. Appendices are regrouped, with several PRISM results moved out of the main text.

P2.justification: The overview figure is replaced and relocated. v2 adds co-adaptation and compression diagrams, training curves, and generation win-rate bars. Benchmark tables are merged or split, PRISM tables move to appendices, new ablation tables appear, and prominent example boxes and an additional PRISM summary example expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The new controls and conversation-only tests in Tables 3–4 strengthen evidence for PLUS's central co-adaptation and flexibility claims, while clearer objectives and fuller PPO settings improve reproducibility. The net gain is limited by conflicting generation sample counts, removed profile-augmentation and controversy-specific evidence, and lost training disclosures. Higher generation win rates use changed evaluation sets and do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.
